newsitem.title: USA: AMR moves ahead with new Miami terminal.
newsitem.headline: AMR moves ahead with new Miami terminal.

text.p: AMR Corp chief executive Robert Crandall said Tuesday the company was ready to move ahead with a new Miami International Airport terminal and has selected veteran aviation management firm Corgan Associates to head its planning and design.
Crandall said at a news conference that it was uncertain when groundbreaking would begin on the terminal, part of a massive $4.6 billion expansion project at the Miami airport.
He said the 47-gate terminal would be the focal point of the airline's plan to create a "major connecting hub" to Europe and Latin America.
"We cannot continue to grow unless we have modern and efficient facilities," Crandall said.

The new terminal was delayed by a challenge by five competing airlines, UAL Corp's United Airlines, Delta Air Lines Inc, US Airways Group Inc, Trans World Airlines Corp and Air Canada, which claimed that the airport's fees structures were unfair.
The companies alleged that they were being asked to subsidize American's terminal.
In March the U.S. Department of Transportation approved Dade County's method for calculating rates and charges, clearly the way for construction of the new facilities.

"Now that the results are in we think it's time for them (American's competitors) to step aside," Crandall said. "We are prepared to pay our full share of the airport's facilities costs and we think our competitors should do the same."
In addition to the 47 jet gates, the facility will have 29 regional aircraft gates for AMR's American Airlines and American Eagle.
Crandall said the project would produce 4,000 construction jobs. American and American Eagle currently have 300 flights a day at MIA and employ 9,300 people in greater Miami.

Crandall said Corgan Associates will oversee the design and planning for the facility and 15 key contractors have been selected for various phases of the project, which is scheduled for completion in 2004.
Jack Corgan, principal partner of Corgan Associates, said the value of the contract with AMR is uncertain.
Privately-held Corgan's most recent project was the $1.5 billion planning and construction of improvements at Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, he said.
